record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.context_brief: Learning topological extinction features with reconstruction
record.original_question: Can persistence or extinction-value features associated with image topology be learned for topological image classification and segmentation by using morphological reconstruction operators, and what architecture should implement the needed iterative reconstruction process, such as a residual architecture, recurrent architecture, or another design?

evidence.quote: Can we learn persistence (extinction values) features to be used in topological image classification and segmentation using morphological operators based on reconstruction? Which architecture to be used for the iterative-based reconstruction (residual, recurrent, other)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In mathematical morphology, given a grayscale image $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ (with $\Omega\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$) and a marker image $g\le f$, the morphological reconstruction by dilation $R_f(g)$ is defined as the limit of the iteration $g_0=g$, $g_{k+1}=(\delta_B(g_k))\wedge f$, where $\delta_B$ is the elementary dilation by a structuring element $B$ and $\wedge$ denotes pointwise minimum; this iteration converges in a finite number of steps to the smallest image $h$ with $g\le h\le f$ that is invariant under $\delta_B(\cdot)\wedge f$. Reconstruction by erosion is defined dually. Using such reconstruction operators one can compute, for every regional maximum (or minimum) $M$ of $f$, its extinction value $\mathrm{ext}(M)$ associated with a measure (volume, dynamics, area), which quantifies the persistence of $M$ under successive morphological filterings; extinction values are closely related to persistent homology of the sublevel/superlevel filtration of $f$ in dimension $0$.

Problem. Design and analyze a trainable deep neural architecture $\mathcal{N}_\theta$, with parameters $\theta$, whose internal computation realizes (or approximates) the iterative morphological reconstruction process $g_{k+1}=(\delta_B(g_k))\wedge f$ with learnable structuring elements / nonlinearities, and whose output produces, for each pixel of an input image $f$, a feature vector encoding the extinction values (equivalently, the $0$-dimensional persistence) of the regional extrema to which it belongs. Specifically:

(a) Prove or disprove that there exists such an architecture for which the learned features are provably consistent estimators of the true extinction values associated with a chosen extinction measure (volume, dynamics, or area), in the sense that as the network depth (number of unrolled reconstruction iterations) tends to infinity the output converges, uniformly on a suitable class of images, to the exact extinction map.

(b) Determine which class of architectures is best suited to implement the unbounded-iteration reconstruction fixed point: a feed-forward residual network of the form $g_{k+1}=g_k+F_\theta(g_k,f)$, a recurrent network sharing weights across iterations, or another design; in particular, characterize necessary and sufficient conditions on $F_\theta$ for the discrete dynamics to converge to $R_f(g)$.

(c) Demonstrate that the resulting persistence/extinction features can be end-to-end trained for topological image classification and semantic segmentation tasks, in the sense that gradients with respect to $\theta$ exist almost everywhere and that minimizing a suitable topological loss based on these features yields segmentations with prescribed Betti numbers.
artifact.status_search_result: Related lines of work exist (differentiable persistent-homology losses for segmentation, topology-preserving deep segmentation, and learnable morphological layers), but no published work appears to provide a unified architecture that learns morphological-reconstruction-based extinction/persistence features through an iterative reconstruction module while characterizing the optimal residual vs. recurrent design. The specific question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Topological Loss Function for Deep-Learning Based Image Segmentation Using Persistent Homology
status_evidence.snippet: Persistent homology is used as a differentiable loss to enforce prescribed Betti numbers in segmentation outputs.
status_evidence.claim: Persistent-homology losses for segmentation exist but do not implement morphological reconstruction inside the network.

status_evidence.title: Topology-Preserving Deep Image Segmentation (NeurIPS 2019)
status_evidence.snippet: A topology-preserving loss using persistent homology trains CNNs whose outputs match ground-truth topology.
status_evidence.claim: Existing topology-aware deep segmentation methods rely on PH losses rather than learned extinction-value features from morphological reconstruction.
